summary: PR #176 (CASSANALYTICS-124) fixes BufferingCommitLogReader.position so CommitLogReader.Result.isFullyRead() turns true. It sets position to the start marker on a seek, to log.maxOffset() on the LEGACY_END_OF_SEGMENT_MARKER (zero-padding) path, and to maxOffset after the segment loop ends normally. The test change is in BufferingCommitLogReaderTests#testReaderSeek. The commit log under test now reports completed()==true. readLog now asserts reader.position()==maxOffset and result.isFullyRead() for both the full read and every re-read from a watermark marker. The class lives only in cassandra-four-zero-bridge, and the test is in the cdc module with a single CassandraBridgeImplementation, so no other bridge is affected. The completed() override is not a mock of the fixed method, because isFullyRead = log.completed() && marker.position >= maxOffset, and the fix targets only the position half. The new assertions would fail on base: a re-read from a marker leaves position at 0, and the padded end-of-segment path leaves it short of maxOffset. Checklists applied: analytics-standards.md '### cass-test-regime' bullets and the DEV-README.md bundle file. Nothing was left unreviewed (tier small).

findings.title: Test the early-termination path that must not set position to maxOffset
findings.rule: Coverage of the change: new branches and error paths exercised
findings.problem: The new `if (statusTracker.shouldContinue())` guards (after readSection and after the loop) exist so that an error or mutation-limit stop leaves position at the last valid offset and isFullyRead() stays false. No test hits that branch. testReaderSeek only reads complete, valid logs, so it asserts position == maxOffset. If the guard were removed or inverted, a reader stopped early by a mutation limit would report fully read and CdcScannerBuilder would skip the rest of the segment. No test would fail.
findings.fix: Add a test that reads with a mutation limit or a corrupt segment and asserts reader.position() < logFile.maxOffset() and result.isFullyRead() is false.
